Nidhi Gupta, J.

The claimants/appellants are before this Court against the dismissal of their claim petition bearing MACT Case No.72 of 28.07.2010 filed by them under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to to as "the Act") by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rupnagar (hereinafter referred to as "the learned Tribunal") vide Award dated 09.11.2011.
09.11.2011 2.
At the very outset, it may be pointed out that the present appeal pertains to the year 2012.

The order sheet reveals that the notice of motion was issued on 09.07.2012;
09.07.2012 and fresh notice was issued to respondent No.4/driver of the alleged offending vehicle on 02.11.2012.

However, respondent No.4 remains unserved unserved till date as the appellants 1 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:018118 have failed to furnish correct address of respondent No.4 despite repeated opportunities.

sentences.text: the appellants to supply correct address of respondent No.4 within a period of three weeks.
The same has not been done till date.
Even no one has appeared on behalf of the appellants today.
Order sheets shows that learned counsel for the appellants had failed to put in appearance on on several dates.
As such, as this is an old matter pertaining to the year 2012, the same is being heard and decided in the absence of learned counsel for the appellants.
3. Learned counsel for the respondents submits that vide the impugned Award, the claim petition of the appellants has been dismissed by citing cogent reasons.
The evidence produced by the parties was considered in great detail.
It was found that the appellants had put up a false case.
The sole alleged eyewitness PW1 was found to be a close friend of the deceased.
Even the said eyewitness had given various contradictory versions of the accident because of which the version of the claimants was disbelieved.

4. Heard.
5.
With the able assistance rendered by learned counsel for the respondents, I have gone through the case file and perused the record in minute detail.

6. Briefly stated the present claim petition was filed by the appellants/5 appellants/ claimants, being the widow, 2 minor children, and 2 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:018118 parents of deceased Sitar Mohammad under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.

Act. It was averred in the claim petition, that on 9.5.2010deceased deceased Sitar Mohammad along-with with Satnam Singh were going to Kurali from village Chuhar Majra on Motor Cycle bearing registration No. PB-10-BS BS-3316 3316 for their personal works.
The Motor Cycle was being driven by Sitar Mohammad at normal speed on correct side of the road.
Satnam Singh was the pillion rider.

When this Motor Cycle reached at TT- point Badali at about 5.30 A.M., then Swaraj Mazda Truck bearing registration No. PB-65-J- PB 9605 (hereinafter referred to as 'the alleged offending vehicle'),being vehicle driven by respondent No. No.4 in rash and negligent manner, all of a sudden was taken towards Badali road without flashing signal in rash and negligent manner, as a result of which the same st struck against the Motor Cycle driven by Sitar Mohammad.
Due to impact or this accident, the head of Sitar Mohammad struck against the body of the Truck.
Both Sitar Mohammad and Satnam Singh fell down on road and sustained grievous injuries.
Truck driver sto stopped the Truck at the spot, but after seeing condition of Sitar Mohammad, he ran away from the spot along with the Truck.
Then Satnam Singh gave telephonic information to police on Mobile Phone No. 100 as a result of which policy party reached at the spot.

Sitar Mohammad and Satnam Singh were shifted to Civil Hospital,
Kurali, but Sitar Mohammad was declared dead by the doctors.
Postmortem on dead body conducted at Civil hospital, Kharar Kharar.

sentences.text: However, the learned Tribunal has found the version put forth by the claimants and PW1 to be doubtful as there are several irreconcilable discrepancies and contradictions in the story put forth by the claimants and their witnesses.
8. As per the version of the claimants, pillion rider Satnam Singh/PW1, is eyewitness to the accident.
FIR No.66 dated 09.05.2010 under Sections 279,337, 304A, 427 IPC was registered on the statement of pillion rider Satnam Singh.
Singh.
However, first and foremost, it has been stated in the FIR that the accident ha had taken place on 9.5.2010 at 5:30 am; but FIR (Ex.P1) was lodged at 8:25 am am.
There is no explanation given for this delay.
9. More importantly, the FIR Ex.P1 records that the accident was caused by unknown vehicle and unknown driver.
Even the Report under Section 173 Cr.P.C. (Ex.PW2/A (Ex.PW2/A), records that the accident was caused by unknown vehicle and unknown driver driver.

It is incomprehensible that if, PW1 Satnam Singh was eyewitness and Pill Pillion Rider to the deceased, how and why did he not know the number of tthe offending vehicle and the identity of the offending driver.

Even further,
there is nothing on record to indicate as to how PW1 and the claimants got this information.
10. Furthermore, it was stated by PW1 in his cross- examination dated 4.2.2011 that the police had trace traced the vehicle and identified the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

However, PW2 4 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:018118 HC Kamaljit Singh IO of case claims that PW1 Satnam Singh disclosed him the number of the vehicle and name of driver on the following day in supplementary mentary statement.
Therefore, diametrically contradictory versions have been given by PW1 and PW2 as to how the name of driver and number of the offending vehicle came into the picture picture.

Moreover, if vehicle had actually been identified by the police, then tthere would be a memo of identification to that effect; and even statement of Satnam Singh would have been recorded by the police regarding such identification.
But that is not so in the present case.
Needless to say, all these factors cast a strong shadow of of doubt on the case put forth by the Claimants.

11. Further in Ex.PW2/A as well as in Ex.P1 it is specifically recorded that the driver of offending vehicle after causing accident fled away from spot due to which number of same could not be read by PW1 PW1.
However, in contradiction thereof, PW1 in his cross cross-examination dated 4.2.2011 has stated that the driver, after stopping the vehicle disembarked for a while, and thereafter fled away.
If away.
If that was so, then PW1 would know the vehicle number as also the identity identity of the driver; and in that event, FIR would not be registered against unknown person and unknown vehicle.
PW1 in his cross-examination cross examination has further categorically stated that he did not see the number of the offending vehicle nor the driver at the spot.
spot. In these facts, there is nothing on record to indicate as to how the driver and the offending vehicle were identified.
However, in his cross cross-examination dated 16.2.2011, PW1 claims to have seen the driver but could not 5 of 7

sentences.text: This would therefore indicate that this version of events had been put up merely to support the claim petition and get compensation.

12. It is the case of the appellants as pleaded in the Grounds of Appeal that the learned Tribunal had failed to consider that the complainant/eyewitness Satnam Singh/PW1 had also received injuries in the accident in question due to which he did not remember the number of the offending vehicle vehicle at the time of the accident.
However, this fact has not been considered by the learned Tribunal.
It has also been pleaded that claim petition has been dismissed only on ground of minor discrepancies.
The learned Tribunal also failed to consider that the deceased was 38 years of age and the parents were dependent upon him and deprived of his love and affection for their entire life.

It is further stated in Para 9 of the Grounds of Appeal that:-
that:
"9.
That ld. Tribunal has wrongly applied the multiplier i.e. 18 and wrongly calculated the dependency should have 1/5th."
13. Needless to say, there is no question of application of multiplier when the claim petition has been dismissed.
Furthermore Furthermore, throughout the record of the case, there is no whisper of any injuries caused to PW1.
This fact has been pleaded for the first time in the present Grounds of Appeal.

Therefore, the Claimants have been unable to establish that the death of Sitar Mohd took place due to the involvement of offending ending vehicle driven by respondent No.4 No.4.
6 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:018118 14.

It has also come on record that Mark-A and Mark-B are the photostat copies of the applications filed by respondent No.4 with SSP Mohali on 02.06.2010.
02.06.2010
Thus, it is obvious that respondent No.4 made representation ion with SSP for complaining of false implication implication.
15. Accordingly, I find no ground is made out to interfere in Award In view of the above, present appeal is dismissed.
the impugned Award.
16. Pending application(s) if any also stand(s) disposed of.
